title: Tag Validator
summary: Given a string representing a code snippet, implement a tag validator to determine if the code is valid according to the following rules: - The code must be enclosed in a valid closed tag.
statement: Given a string representing a code snippet, implement a tag validator to determine if the code is valid according to the following rules: - The code must be enclosed in a valid closed tag. - A closed tag has a start tag and an end tag , where TAG_NAME is the same in both tags. - A valid TAG_NAME consists of uppercase letters and has a length between 1 and 9 characters. - TAG_CONTENT can include other valid closed tags, CDATA sections, and any characters, except for unmatched tags or invalid TAG_NAME. - An unmatched to be valid. - CDATA sections are denoted by and should be treated as regular text, ignoring any tags within them.
constraints: The whole code must be one closed root tag.
Tag names contain 1–9 uppercase letters; CDATA is recognized only inside an open tag and ends at the first ]]> marker.
hints: A stack enforces properly nested tag names while a dedicated branch skips complete CDATA regions.
Scan left to right, rejecting content outside the one root.
Push start names, match and pop end names, skip from <![CDATA[ to ]]>, and validate names.
The stack is exactly the unmatched ancestor chain, and every special opening token is consumed according to its grammar.
editorial: The stack is exactly the unmatched ancestor chain, and every special opening token is consumed according to its grammar.

tests.explanation: A single matching uppercase root tag is valid.
CDATA shields its apparent nested tag text from parsing.
